body:
THE RERUN CAME BACK GREEN. NONDETERMINISM IS PROVEN, AND THIS IS THE RESULT I TOLD YOU I WOULD BE MOST TEMPTED TO UNDER-REPORT, SO I AM LEADING WITH IT.

    run 35663002466, workflow CI
    attempt 1   FAILED   scaffold_refresh::tests::starter_role_refresh_adds_missing_prompt_and_preserves_user_prompt
    attempt 2   SUCCESS  Build (ubuntu-latest)
    sha         bfef2601b1e7  ON BOTH ATTEMPTS
    PR head     bfef2601b1e7... unchanged, so the comparison is valid

Same commit, same code, same workflow, opposite outcomes. The branch never moved - I re-checked the PR head after the result rather than trusting that the freeze held. Your instruction to the lane to hold its push is what made this readable.

SO IT IS THE FIRST BRANCH OF YOUR FORK, NOT THE SECOND. The test is nondeterministic. It is NOT the bigger finding - an unrelated one-commit delta turning that test red - and I want to be plain that the bigger finding would have been the more interesting one and it did not happen. #2065's red Build was not the implementer's doing, which the merge-base argument already suggested and this now settles.

THE SYMMETRIC LIMIT, BECAUSE IT IS THE SAME DISCIPLINE THAT GOT US HERE. One red run was not evidence of nondeterminism. ONE GREEN AFTER ONE RED IS NOT EVIDENCE OF A RATE. A single contradiction is sufficient to prove nondeterminism - that is why this experiment was cheap and decisive - but n=1 on each side says nothing about whether this test fails one run in three or one in fifty. If the flake rate matters for deciding whether to chase it, that needs a population, and nothing we have touches it.

WHAT IS STILL UNKNOWN, STATED AS UNKNOWN. THE MECHANISM. I ruled out the unlocked-env race and the stale base; neither was it. I have no candidate now. The test does filesystem work under a tempdir and sets HOME/AIDA_TEST_HOME through the lock, and something about that is order- or timing-sensitive, but I have not identified what and I am not going to guess at it in a verdict. Whether it is worth chasing is yours - a confirmed-flaky test in the required Build job is a real cost, because it turns every red into a question rather than an answer, which is exactly what it cost us here.

WHAT I WOULD NOT DO: retry-annotate it. That converts a known-flaky test into an invisible one, and by this afternoon's taxonomy it is the third limb again - a failure that reports the success value. The honest interim state is "known flaky, mechanism unidentified, tracked", not a green that means less than it appears to.

VERDICT UNCHANGED: #2065 stays CHANGES REQUESTED at bfef2601b1 on F1 (Custom edges vanish from the spec card - your count, 1480+), F2 (criterion 2, reasoning not recorded on the spec) and F3 (criterion 3, the 103 inert edges stranded silently). All three are about the diff and none of them moved.

The lane can push now as far as I am concerned - the experiment is finished and its result is recorded.

BOARD: #2066 APPROVED at ac772eaca9 and ready to merge on its stated condition (its own doc gates were suppressed by BUG-1578, harmless for that document). #2065 and #2019 correctly refused and held. #2067 not routed to me; the `.codex/hooks/` gap is in your inbox.
subject: RERUN GREEN at the same sha — nondeterminism PROVEN (attempt 1 red, attempt 2 green, bfef2601b1 both). Mechanism still unknown, and one green is not a rate
